Euer Wohlgeborn

Kontop den 31ten August

1809.

translation.en: Your Honour, Highly Honoured Sir Court Councillor. Your Honour's most highly esteemed letter I received today by express; my joy was at first without bounds, to know you as my cousin in Breiten, but upon reading your friendly letter further a new sorrow stunned my heart, so that I could scarcely compose myself. I have a plan by which I may be rescued out of all embarras, only 1800 Rthl of interest must be paid; before that I cannot come to Breslau or into those parts. Honour and fortune are still not at stake there. I am at present, through the one accursed v. d. Lahr affair, dreadfully disgraced, and cannot show myself there any sooner than when the 1800 Rthl of interest are paid. Then I can appear there and carry out my plan. If the Most Serene Lord does not help me with this trifle, then may God stand by my forsaken children; I shall then go to another place where I shall not have need of His Serene Highness's help. I have sent His Serene Highness the letter of my daughter, which she wrote in despair, after the distraint on account of the v. d. Lahr debt, to my youngest son, so that such a cry of lamentation might move the Lord; if he does not help me with the trifle, then all gentle feelings have ever been strangers to him. Dear friend - it is 1800 Rthl that can save me from shame and mockery, indeed from ruin; these determine my choice or my dwelling - I must have them, for otherwise I shall not come there - Should the

Prince rescue me thereby, then I shall appear there justified - but not, either, without a summons. I shall then carry through my cause with honour - dismember a part of my estates, assign my children the interest for their maintenance, and then go to the King, where I shall remain until much has been accomplished. This is my plan, and these are the consequences, if the Prince finds means regarding the 1800 Rthl - Should this last not come to pass, then I can no longer present myself there, but shall go to Königsberg and from there perhaps into hell. My heart could burst when I consider my misfortune, which I suffer so undeservedly. Here the estates are, through the bruit which I endured in Berlin on account of the eternal Lahr affair, placed under sequestration; there now swum across, however - but where shall I turn? Schweineren can be saved with 1800 Rthl, and I be put in a position to carry out all plans - Here too it would prepare beneficial consequences. One would deal more sparingly with me if I had Schweine free again; thus everything there depends upon the speedy help of Her Serene Highness. I would gladly sacrifice for it in return my whole blessedness of life and all else, if only the Lord will do this for me. Take thought, Your Honour, therefore, if it is in the world possible for you, and find means soon, for then I can depart from here on the 12th of September so as to be in Schlawenschutz about the 16th - but without this help I forsake everything. With a grateful heart and true high esteem I shall ever be Your Honour's, Kontop, the 31st of August 1809, truly devoted friend and servant v Triebenfeld

summary_en: A desperate personal appeal to the Court Councillor: 1800 Rthl of interest must be found, or the writer cannot show himself in Breslau, disgraced as he is by the v. d. Lahr affair and the distraint that drove his daughter to write in despair. With the sum, Schweineren could be freed, his estates partly dismembered, interest assigned to his children, and his cause pressed before the King; without it, Königsberg and abandonment of all. Estates here lie under sequestration; departure planned for 12 September, Schlawenschutz by the 16th.
summary_de: Verzweifelte Bitte um 1800 Rthl Zinsen, ohne die eine Reise nach Breslau bzw. Schlawenschutz unmöglich sei: die v. d. Lahr-Sache habe ihn nach dem Berliner Gerede öffentlich entehrt und zur Sequestration der Güter geführt; mit der Summe ließe sich Schweineren retten und sein Plan ausführen – Teilung der Güter, Zinsen zum Unterhalt der Kinder, Reise zum König. Ein in Verzweiflung geschriebener Brief der Tochter sei dem Fürsten übersandt; bleibe die Hilfe aus, gehe er nach Königsberg. Abreise am 12. September, Ankunft um den 16.
